frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Self-manifesting radiance: an active source or emission that makes itself and its surroundings perceptible through glow/light. Lexicalized three ways in the corpus: nār = the radiant (combusting) entity itself; nūr = the emitted/received radiance; munīr (Form IV) = imparting radiance.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: Self-manifesting radiance: an active source or emission that makes itself and its surroundings perceptible through glow/light. Lexicalized three ways in the corpus: nār = the radiant (combusting) entity itself; nūr = the emitted/received radiance; munīr (Form IV) = imparting radiance.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: All 194 occurrences token one of three lexemes — nār "fire" (~145), nūr "light" (~43), munīr "radiance-giving" (6) — and each one names something whose defining property is that it shows itself by glowing. Fire in this corpus is consistently the seen, kindled, blazing entity: Moses perceives it from afar as a beacon (20:10, 27:7, 28:29), it illuminates its surroundings (2:17), molten iron becomes "fire" exactly when it glows (18:96), a sacrifice's acceptance is signaled by fire visibly consuming it (3:183). Light (nūr) is radiance detached from combustion: the moon (10:5, 71:16), God's light (24:35), revelation (5:15, 42:52), the believers' light running before them (57:12, 66:8), always opposed to darkness (2:257, 6:1). The bridge is internal: in 2:17 a kindled nār "illuminates" and its output is immediately called their nūr; in 24:35 nār and nūr co-occur in one radiance economy ("light upon light"). One root, one contribution: radiant self-manifestation; whether it burns (nār) or only shines (nūr) is lexeme- and context-level elaboration.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: ROOT residue = radiant self-manifestation. LEXEME layer: nār adds combustive embodiment (heat, fuel, consuming — cf. waqūd 2:24, 85:5; lahab 111:3), nūr adds pure emission/reception without heat (moon = nūr while sun = sirāj/ḍiyāʾ, 71:16, 10:5 — a deliberate internal contrast showing nūr excludes blaze). FORM layer: Form IV munīr adds causation — imparting radiance to others (kitāb munīr, sirāj munīr, qamar munīr). CONSTRUCTION layer: definite al-nār + idafa (nār jahannam, nār Allāh) builds the eschatological proper-noun usage; ẓulumāt→nūr prepositional frames build the guidance schema. CONTEXT layer: punishment, theophany (27:8), cosmology, and soteriology are all contextual deployments; none alters the residue. Crucially, heat is shown detachable from the root (21:69: fire commanded to be cool yet still addressed yā-nāru) while radiance is never detached anywhere in the corpus.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 2:174 (with parallel 4:10): "they eat nothing into their bellies but al-nār" — fire located inside bellies, unseen, where visible radiance seems absent and only harm/consumption is in view. Resolution: the root supplies the inherently radiant entity, and the construction is a disclosure claim — what they swallow IS (already, in reality) the Fire that will manifest; concealment-now is the rhetorical point (katama 'concealing' is the very sin named in the verse), and the eschatological manifestation is explicit in the sequel (wa-sayaṣlawna saʿīran, 4:10). The token still denotes the radiant entity, deployed as latent. This is the hardest case; it bends but does not break the residue.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Burning heat / combustion as the root core. Falsified internally: (1) all ~43 nūr tokens involve no heat — the moon is nūr while the sun is separately sirāj/ḍiyāʾ (71:16, 10:5), and believers' light, God's light, and scripture-light are heatless; (2) 21:69 subtracts heat from a nār by decree ("be coolness and peace") while the entity remains nār; (3) 9:81 predicates heat of the Fire (ashaddu ḥarran) as an attribute, showing heat is asserted about it, not constitutive of the name; (4) 18:96 applies nār to glowing metal with no combustion. A second competitor — generic 'manifestation/visibility' — is too broad: it cannot explain why every token is specifically visual-radiant (glow, kindling, illumination, darkness-opposition), never mere appearance.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from nearest neighbors, all attested in-corpus alongside nwr: w-q-d = the act/state of kindling and fuel (istawqada 2:17, yūqidūna 13:17, waqūd 2:24) — nwr is the radiant entity kindled, not the kindling; ḍ-w-ʾ = the illuminating effect on surroundings (aḍāʾat 2:17, ḍiyāʾ 10:5) — nwr is the source/emission, not the effect-event; s-r-j / ṣ-b-ḥ = the lamp-vessel artifact (24:35, 25:61); l-h-b = the flame-tongue (111:3); s-ʿ-r / j-ḥ-m = blaze-intensity terms for the Fire; ẓ-l-m (ẓulumāt) = the systematic antonym. 2:17 alone stacks four of these layers (istawqada / nāran / aḍāʾat / nūrihim), letting the corpus itself isolate the nwr slot: the self-radiant thing and its radiance. Falsifiable: a token of nār with luminosity denied while the name holds, or a nūr with no visual-radiance framing, would break it; none exists in the 194.
internal_discovery.rationale: Full coverage: all 194 confirmed occurrences were individually assessed (145 nār, 43 nūr, 6 munīr). The proposed residue — self-manifesting radiance — survives subtraction of lexeme, form, construction, and context in every token, with zero irreconcilable cases. The result is STRONG rather than merely plausible because the corpus supplies its own unification evidence: bridge verses where fire's output is named nūr (2:17) or where nār and nūr transact in one image (24:35), boundary cases where the name nār tracks glow rather than heat or combustion (18:96, 21:69), and a systematic division of labor with neighboring roots (w-q-d, ḍ-w-ʾ, s-r-j, l-h-b, ẓ-l-m) that leaves exactly the radiant-source slot to nwr. The hardest case (2:174, fire hidden in bellies) is a rhetorical latency deployment, not a residue failure. No occurrence was forced; nothing here is canonical.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Full coverage read (194/194). Every occurrence denotes fire (nAr), light (nUr), or a luminous source (munIr), so a UNIFIED nwr sense ("a self-manifesting fire/light source") is present across the whole set — hence not REFUTED. But the PROPOSED wording overreaches on two of the three tested criteria, so not SUPPORTED.

(A) Universal presence of the specific residue fails. The proposal's unifying thread is "radiance … makes itself AND ITS SURROUNDINGS perceptible through glow/light." That radiance/illumination component is NOT demonstrably grounded in the heat/torment-salient nAr subset — the verse evidence there gives heat/scorching/branding or location/punishment, not glow: 101:11 (nArun HAmiyah, scorching), 88:4 (nAran HAmiyah), 9:81 (nAru jahannama ashaddu Harran, hotter), 55:35 (shuwAZ min nAr wa-nuHAs, flame + molten copper), 15:27 (nAr al-samUm, scorching fire of the jAnn), 9:35 (yuHmA … fa-tukwA, heated for branding). Pure abode/torment formulas ground location, not illumination: 6:128 (al-nAru mathwAkum), 57:15 (al-nAru hiya mawlAkum), 41:28 (al-nAr … dAr al-khuld), 4:145 (al-dark al-asfal min al-nAr), 40:72 (fI l-nAri yusjarUn). The proposal only saves these by re-glossing nAr as "combusting entity," which silently swaps the residue from RADIANCE to COMBUSTION(heat+light) — an internal inconsistency that voids the single-thread "radiance" claim. So the residue that is truly universal is the broader "fire/light source," not the narrower "perceptible-through-glow radiance" as stated.

(B) Distinctiveness fails (distinctiveness_ok=false). The corpus itself separates nUr from raw radiance: 10:5 gives the SUN DiyA' (Dw') and the MOON nUr in one verse; 71:16 gives the sun sirAj (srj) and the moon nUr. If the residue were "an active self-manifesting source that makes surroundings perceptible through glow," that better describes DiyA'/sirAj (the intrinsically radiant sun/lamp) than nUr (the milder/derived moonlight the corpus deliberately labels nUr). The residue is thus not cleanly separable from nearest roots Dw' and srj (and on the nAr side from wqd/lhb/sVr/Hrr, which the corpus pairs with nAr: waqUd 2:24/66:6/85:5, yUqad 24:35, mUqadah 104:6, talaZZA 92:14).

(C) Falsifiable=true: the claim predicts every token is a fire/light source and would be refuted by a non-luminous, non-combusting nwr token; none exists, so the weak unity survives, but the proposed formulation's radiance-through-line and distinctiveness do not.

Verdict rationale: under non-negotiable unity, the presence of heat-only / abode-only nAr occurrences that do not demonstrably carry the proposed "radiance/perceptibility" residue (only combustion-heat or location) blocks SUPPORTED; the genuine cross-set unity of a fire/light source plus the failed distinctiveness lands this at PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. A defensible SUPPORTED-grade residue would need re-wording to "an energetic self-manifesting source of fire-or-light" AND an explicit account of why nUr (not DiyA') is selected for the moon.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Under QAC canonical numbering (basmala excluded from verse-1 word count), 14:1:10:2 resolves to word 10 seg 2 = نُّورِ (nūr), which fits the frozen contribution cleanly: the verse brings people out of ẓulumāt (darkness) into an-nūr (radiance) = emitted/received radiance. However, the shard's verse_text prepends the 4-token basmala (بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ), so a naive token-position count over the rendered text lands word 10 on ٱلنَّاسَ (nās, root n-w-s), not نُور. This offset between the canonical morphological index (→نُور) and the rendered-text token position (→نَّاس) is a basmala token-position artifact, which per protocol is STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY — the semantic fit is genuine but the mapping is structurally contaminated by the basmala offset, so it is neither forced to CONSISTENT nor genuinely RESISTANT.

Data artifact: verse_text prepends the basmala while the token index (position 9 = wa-al-nur) is counted without it; does not block judgment — the sole نور in the verse (wa-al-nur, opposed to al-zulumat) unambiguously = emitted radiance/light. Consistent.
